## Overview Block-outermost layouts pack Mamba states into blocks at their own page size (`_get_packed_kv_cache_groups`), so padding the Mamba page to the attention page only lowers the number of states per block. This drops that padding when the attention backends support only block-outermost layouts, and lets a packed Mamba group widen the block by up to one state when that saves a group. #55449, stacked on this PR, corrects the block size for packed ds_mla caches; the two change disjoint configurations. ## Claims - `_align_hybrid_block_size` skips the Mamba padding when every layout from `get_supported_kv_cache_layouts` is block-outermost. - `_get_packed_kv_cache_groups` lets a Mamba group take one more state than the block fits, which widens the block only when that saves a group. Like main's split, this depends only on the specs, so NIXL P/D peers that differ in `max_model_len`, prefix caching or TP still get the same plan; a bytes-per-request check would not. - GLM-5.3-Flash with MTP off and an fp8 or bf16 MLA cache: 4 → 3 KDA groups, up to +26% max concurrency. SM90 bf16 at 128k without prefix caching loses up to 1.5%, and 20 of 192 configurations at 512k/1M lose up to 2.6%. - GLM-5.3-Flash on GB10 with an `fp8_ds_mla` cache and a DFlash2 drafter, whose sliding-window layers the CPU grid does not model: 9 → 6 KV cache groups, +24% max concurrency at 404,992 tokens. ## Validation GLM-5.3-Flash (real `config.json`) through the allocation path on CPU, 960 configurations: max concurrency is higher in 140, lower in 4 (SM90 bf16 TP1/2 at 128k without prefix caching, down to −1.5%), unchanged in the rest, including every `fp8_ds_mla` one.
Max concurrency vs main (main 8530a778f7, this PR ff05114cd2) SM90/SM100/SM120 × TP 1/2/4/8 × MTP 0/1/3/5 × 8k/32k/128k × prefix caching on/off × 8/40 GiB KV cache per GPU: | platform | `--kv-cache-dtype` | configs | better | equal | worse | max | |---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | SM90 | `fp8` | 192 | 48 | 144 | 0 | +25.6% | | SM90 | `auto` (bf16) | 192 | 44 | 144 | 4 | +21.5% | | SM90 | `fp8_ds_mla` | 192 | 0 | 192 | 0 | 0% | | SM100 | `fp8` | 192 | 48 | 144 | 0 | +25.9% | | SM120 | `auto` (→ `fp8_ds_mla`) | 192 | 0 | 192 | 0 | 0% | At 512k/1M: 76 of 192 better (up to +3.1%), 20 worse (down to −2.6%), all with MTP off.
```bash pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_planning.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner.py -k "glm5_like_hybrid or hybrid_mla_block_alignment" ``` All four pass; `test_packed_groups_glm5_like_hybrid[12288]` and the `KpoolTailBackend` row of `test_hybrid_mla_block_alignment` fail on main. GB10 (SM121), GLM-5.3-Flash NVFP4, TP2, 8 GiB KV cache per GPU, main `8530a778f7` vs this PR `ff05114cd2`: with the production serve config, whose DFlash2 drafter adds sliding-window attention layers next to the `fp8_ds_mla` cache, main pads the Mamba page and needs 9 KV cache groups, this PR 6, and max concurrency at 404,992 tokens rises from 1.97x to 2.45x. The MTP configurations match the CPU harness exactly, and GSM8K is unchanged.
GB10 runs Capacity from the startup log (dummy weights; KV sizing does not depend on them): | config | main | this PR | |---|---|---| | production: `fp8` KV with sliding-window layers skipped, DFlash2 (`incoai/GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2`, 7 tokens), 404,992 | 9 groups, 796,748 tokens, 1.97x | 6 groups, 991,077 tokens, 2.45x | | `auto` (→ `fp8_ds_mla`), MTP 3, 8k | block 4608, 5 groups, 13.14x | same | | `auto`, MTP 5, 128k | block 4608, 5 groups, 5.11x | same | GSM8K (lm-eval `gsm8k`, 5-shot, first 500 questions, greedy) with real weights, production serve config at 8k context and 16 sequences: main 0.910, this PR 0.924 (strict match, ± 0.013). Greedy outputs are not reproducible across server starts here (two main starts: 1 of 13 code prompts identical); main vs this PR is within that.
## Details - With the padding, GLM-5.3-Flash's block holds 11 KDA states, so its 34 KDA layers need 4 groups; without it, or with the extra state, 12 fit. Dropping the padding alone improves 96 configurations, both changes together 140. - Only GLM-5.3-Flash (KPOOL tail cache) and Qwen4Exp with QSA side caches skip the padding today; Qwen4Exp is not measured. - Related: RFC #58638 question 2 asks how to size blocks for block-outermost layouts; this keeps the alignment's block and changes only how Mamba states fill it. #56156 skips the alignment for opt-in layer-wise KV caches. #60996 restructures the same Mamba split (textual conflict) and keeps the Mamba padding. AI-assisted contribution (Claude Code); I reviewed every changed line. ---
Pull Request Checklist - [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans). - [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR. - [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity. - [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI. - [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples. - [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
